analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md is changed; the supplied units are BASE text, lines 218-663, of the pre-change changelog. Per the file_changes patch excerpt, the head side rewrites the top of the file with a v0.10.0 candidate section, and the base entries shown are mostly carried forward. No executable code, configuration, workflow or schema changes are visible in these units, so no code path, control or trust boundary is altered by the supplied evidence.

I checked the changelog prose against the retained threat model for claims that could invalidate documented assumptions. The cache-reliability entry (base lines 327-329) strips caller-supplied user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies. That is consistent with T-041, where the coordinator authors cacheSalt from authenticated account, model build and prompt contract, and caller prompt_cache_key and user fields do not participate. The prompt normalization v8 and v9 notes (base lines 432 and the head upgrade note) say prompt_contract_id changes, caches start cold, and the coordinator attaches a cache scope only when the advertised contract matches. This fails toward no cache reuse rather than cross-scope reuse, so it adds no leak. The SSD cache entries (write budget at 588-590, the MiMo cache defaults at 499-502) leave unchanged the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup tags and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch described in T-041. The frozen legacy MDM and App Attest entries (base lines 331-342) are consistent with TB-011 and T-052, T-053 and T-057: App Attest authorization is required, there is no grace expiry, and failure is fail-closed.

Limits: the head text beyond the excerpt, including the v0.10.0 section, is not supplied in these units. Any behavior it describes is documentation only. The actual code, such as the MLX and mlx-swift-lm submodule bumps, was not reviewed here. The documented kernel and metallib changes and the Flint, Nemotron and GLM model additions would need review in the source diffs if those are part of this PR. No findings qualify from the changelog alone.
